title: The JSON objects the dermixen command prints
description: Every command prints exactly one of these objects on standard output when given --json. The definition named after a command is the shape of that command's output; the others are shared parts.

hash.description: The BLAKE3 hash of a file's bytes as sixty-four lowercase hexadecimal digits.

key.description: The tonic and mode, such as A minor or F# major.

year_is_approximate.description: True when the year is an estimate taken from a release's other tracks or from other work by the same artists, rather than a year some source states.

release.description: What Discogs says about the release a track came from. A scan never fills these, because tags name the pressing a file was ripped from rather than the release the music first appeared on.

data_source.description: Which lookup answered, or null when no match has been recorded.

loudness.description: The EBU R 128 measurement volume leveling uses, as docs/library.md describes under `loudness`.

integrated_lufs.description: The integrated loudness of the whole track, in loudness units relative to full scale.

true_peak_db.description: The highest true peak in either channel, in decibels relative to full scale.

track_record.description: Everything the library knows about one track, as docs/library.md describes.

phrases.description: Null when the record was written before phrases were stored or the analyzer failed on the track.

loudness.description: Null when the record has no loudness measurement or the track has no measurable loudness.

decode.description: The output of `dermixen decode --json`: the file decoded and the WAV written.

file.description: The audio file decoded, as its canonical path.

from_seconds.description: Where in the file the WAV begins.

length_samples.description: How many frames the WAV contains.

analyze.description: The output of `dermixen analyze --json`: the record the library would store for the file.

library.description: The library file the scan wrote to.

completed.description: How many records that had no loudness were completed with one.

library_query.description: The output of `dermixen library query --json`: the matching records in ascending order of path.

library_find.description: The output of `dermixen library find --json`: the best matches first.

mix.description: The mix document the window was opened on, as an absolute path with symbolic links resolved.

app.description: The window's executable that was started.

pid.description: The process ID of the window.

mix_show.description: The output of `dermixen mix show --json` and of `dermixen mix add --json`: the mix laid out on the timeline.

length_samples.description: The length of the rendered mix.

position.description: The track's place in the playlist, counting from one.

gain_db.description: The gain applied to the whole track, as docs/project-file.md describes under "The gain".

start_seconds.description: When the track's first sample is heard, counted from the start of the rendered mix.

end_seconds.description: When the track's last sample has been heard, counted the same way.

mix_plan.description: The output of `dermixen mix plan --json`: the timeline `mix add` would build from the playlist, laid out as mix_show lays a document out, with the names, the key, and the tempo step a person plans by, and every warning the plan earned.

length_samples.description: The length the rendered mix would have.

keys_checked.description: Whether the keys were checked. They are not when the median key confidence across the library is under a tenth, because the Camelot codes are then noise and a clash between two of them means nothing.

warnings.description: Every warning the plan earned, one sentence each, which the command also writes on standard error: a tempo step over the limit, two keys that do not fit, or an artist on more than one track.

position.description: The track's place in the playlist, counting from one.

gain_db.description: The gain applied to the whole track, as docs/project-file.md describes under "The gain".

start_seconds.description: When the track's first sample is heard, counted from the start of the rendered mix.

end_seconds.description: When the track's last sample has been heard, counted the same way.

artist.description: The artist the library records for the track, or null when it records none.

title.description: The title the library records for the track, or null when it records none.

camelot.description: The track's Camelot code, or null when the library records no key.

tempo_step_bpm.description: This track's tempo minus the tempo of the track before it, which is how far the mix tempo moves at the transition into this track. Null for the first track.

mix_relink.description: The output of `dermixen mix relink --json`: what became of each track's file.

relinked.description: How many tracks now name a new path.

missing.description: How many tracks still have no file.

position.description: The track's place in the playlist, counting from one.

path.description: The path the document names now.

from.description: The path the document named before, for a relinked track; null otherwise.

reason.description: Where the file was looked for, for a missing track; null otherwise.

render.description: The output of `dermixen render --json`. With `--handover`, the `handover` object says where the handover falls in the clip written.

path.description: The WAV or MP3 file written.

handover.description: Present when the render was asked for with `--handover N`: the clip around the handover into track N.

into_track.description: The track the handover goes into, counting from one.

from_seconds.description: Where the clip starts, counted from the start of the mix as `mix show` counts it.

rise_seconds.description: Where the incoming track's rise begins, thirty-two beats before its intro anchor, counted from the start of the clip.

anchor_seconds.description: Where the two anchors meet, counted from the start of the clip.

outgoing_end_seconds.description: Where the outgoing track's last sample is heard, counted from the start of the clip.

capture.description: The WAV file the frames were written to instead of a device, or null when they were played.

from_seconds.description: Where playing began, counted from the start of the mix.

mix_length_seconds.description: The length of the whole mix, as mix show reports it.

underruns.description: How many times the device needed frames that were not ready. Zero means the mix was heard without a gap.

scoreboard.description: The output of `dermixen scoreboard --json`: one row per analyzer for beats and for keys, and, when the directory holds anchor annotations, for anchors, for grids, and for phrases, each with its per-track scores.

confidence.description: How sure the analyzer was, from zero to one, when it answered.

anchors.description: One row per anchor analyzer per label source, present only when the ground truth holds anchor annotations.

source.description: The label source the scoreboard measured the analyzer against for this row, or null for all sources together.

grids.description: One row per beat analyzer scored against the labeled grids, present only when the ground truth holds anchor annotations.

first_beat.description: The beat of the labeled grid at which the analyzer's beat zero fell.

source.description: The label source the scoreboard measured the analyzer against for this row, or null for all sources together.

downbeat.description: The share of tracks whose bar lines are the labeled ones; only the row over all sources has it.

settings.description: The output of `dermixen settings show --json`, `settings set --json`, and `settings reset --json`: every setting as it stands after the command.

file.description: The settings file, whether or not it exists.

audio_buffer_frames.description: How many frames the audio device takes per pull.

value.description: The number of frames, or null when the device's own size is used.

set.description: Whether the file sets this setting.

metronome.description: Whether the grid editor's metronome is on.

value.description: Whether the metronome is on: the setting, or false when the file does not set it.

set.description: Whether the file sets this setting.

grid_strip_collapsed.description: Whether the grid editor's strip, the waveform with the grid drawn over it, is collapsed.

value.description: Whether the strip is collapsed: the setting, or false when the file does not set it.

set.description: Whether the file sets this setting.

library_collapsed.description: Whether the library panel beside the timeline is hidden, so the timeline has the whole width of the window.

value.description: Whether the panel is hidden: the setting, or false when the file does not set it.

set.description: Whether the file sets this setting.

library_word_wrap.description: Whether the text in a library panel cell wraps onto further lines.

value.description: Whether a cell's text wraps: the setting, or false when the file does not set it.

set.description: Whether the file sets this setting.

music_folder.description: The folder the person's music is in, which a scan reads when it is given no folder.

value.description: The folder in use, as a path in full: the setting, below the user's home folder when the setting is a relative path, or Music/Undefunktis below the home folder when the file does not set it.

set.description: Whether the file sets this setting.

library_file.description: The library file the window and the library commands open when neither --library nor DERMIXEN_LIBRARY_FILE names one.

value.description: The file in use, as a path in full: the setting, below the user's home folder when the setting is a relative path, or dermixen/library.sqlite below the user's data folder when the file does not set it.

set.description: Whether the file sets this setting.

error.description: How far the analyzer's position sits from the label, in beats; negative when early.

phrase_record.description: What the phrase analyzer found in a track: which beat of every four starts a bar, the bars that start phrases, and the bars at which the arrangement changes. Every beat is a whole beat of the record's grid, which is not moved.

downbeat.description: Bars begin at every beat that is this many beats past a whole multiple of four.

bars.description: The longest phrase that begins at this bar.
